title: Chapter 54 — Association Networking
intro: Using industry associations as systematic business development platforms — NKBA, HBA, and local design communities.

sections.title: The Associations That Matter
sections.content:
NKBA — National Kitchen & Bath Association. This is where the designers are. Join the local chapter. Attend monthly meetings. Volunteer for a committee. The rep who shows up consistently for 6 months becomes a familiar face. The one who shows up once is forgotten.

Local Home Builders Association (HBA/BILD). This is where the builders and contractors are. Their events, golf tournaments, and trade shows are prospecting goldmines if you approach them as relationship-building, not selling.

Local design guilds, decorator associations, and architecture firms often host networking events. These are smaller, more intimate, and often more productive than large association events.

sections.title: Networking That Produces
sections.content:
The goal of every association event is not to sell. It is to earn one meeting. Hand out cards, but more importantly, collect cards. Ask what projects they are working on. Listen for the appliance moment — 'We are doing a kitchen in a new build on River Road' — and offer to help.

Follow up within 48 hours. 'Great meeting you at the NKBA event last night. You mentioned the River Road project — I would love to put together some spec options for you. Can I send them over?'

The event is the opening. The follow-up is the selling.

sections.title: Becoming a Resource
sections.content:
The highest-value position in any association is being the go-to appliance resource. Offer to present on topics the membership cares about: new product trends, ventilation code changes, panel-ready integration best practices, energy efficiency updates.

A 15-minute presentation to 30 designers is 30 warm introductions. Compare that to 30 cold calls. The conversion rate is not even close.

The long game: after a year of consistent involvement, you will have a reputation in the design and building community. Prospects will come to you. That is the goal.
